newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cabinet delays energy VAT increase vote.
newsitem.headline: Czech cabinet delays energy VAT increase vote.

text.p: The Czech cabinet delayed final debate until next week on increasing value added tax (VAT) on electricity and natural gas to 22 percent from five percent, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Wednesday.

"The definitive negotiations on the VAT will be held next week," Dlouhy told a news conference after a cabinet meeting. He said debate was postponed in order to consider subsidies for low-income households put under strain by the VAT increase and price deregulations.

The planned change, which would also need approval in parliament as a change in the tax code, would take effect on July 1. It has already been agreed in principle by leaders of the three parties in the centre-right ruling coalition.
The hike in VAT is in part a revenue enhancer to help the Finance Ministry ward off a feared deficit in the 1997 budget because of slower than expected economic growth.
The ministry on Tuesday reported a 6.7 billion crown shortfall through the end of February.

Both the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, the senior coalition party, and Dlouhy's pro-business Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) support an overall 35 percent rise in energy prices for this year.
The parties had been split before the talks last week on the VAT increase. Coalition leaders have said they will meet next week to discuss a further rise beyond the VAT hike.
